rationales: Bu Ali Sina is not credited with writing Al-Haywan.
Aristotle wrote works on animals, but Al-Haywan is attributed here to Jabir Bin Hayan.
Abdul Malik Asmai wrote works about animals, but not the book asked for.
Jabir Bin Hayan is credited with writing Al-Haywan.
Aristotle studied nature but did not form the theory of evolution described here.
Darwin developed his theory of evolution after studying the works of other naturalists.
Laveran is known for discovering the malaria parasite, not for forming the theory of evolution.
Ronald Ross is known for work on malaria transmission, not for forming the theory of evolution.
Monera are prokaryotic organisms, not eukaryotic multicellular consumers.
Protista are mostly unicellular and are not the kingdom of multicellular consumers.
Plantae are primarily multicellular producers, not consumers.
Animalia includes eukaryotic multicellular consumers.
Ribosomes use rRNA but are not the sites where it is formed.
Mitochondria are not the usual site of cellular rRNA formation asked about here.
The nucleolus is where ribosomal RNA is formed.
Vacuoles do not form ribosomal RNA.
Germ-line cells can undergo mitosis, but they are not the only cells that do so.
Prokaryotic cells divide by binary fission rather than mitosis.
Mitosis occurs in eukaryotic cells.
Bacteria are prokaryotes and do not undergo mitosis.
Ribosome synthesis is not the key process identified here as necessary for entry into mitosis.
Inhibiting protein synthesis in G2 prevents production of proteins needed for mitosis.
Chromosome duplication occurs in S phase, not G2.
Enzyme synthesis is not the specific process identified here as necessary for entry into mitosis.
Vitamins are not the products of lipid digestion by lipase.
Lipase digests lipids into fatty acids and glycerol.
Glycogen is not a product of lipid digestion.
Glucose is produced by carbohydrate digestion, not lipid digestion.
About 1% is not the stated proportion of light absorbed by the leaf surface.
About 2% of the light falling on the leaf surface is absorbed.
About 3% is not the stated proportion of light absorbed by the leaf surface.
About 15% is much higher than the stated proportion absorbed.
Arteries generally do not have valves along their length to prevent backflow.
Veins have valves that help prevent blood from flowing backward.
Capillaries do not have valves.
Muscles are not blood vessels and do not contain valves for blood flow.
Milk is not described as having 10% lipid in this context.
Milk is not described as having 12% lipid in this context.
0.9% is not the stated lipid content of milk.
Milk contains about 4% lipid.
Loss of electrons is oxidation.
Reduction involves gaining electrons.
Dehydration is the removal of water, not the loss of an electron.
Respiration is a cellular energy-releasing process, not the name for electron loss.
Jabir Bin Hayan is not credited with first giving the concept of metabolism here.
Koshland is associated with the induced-fit model of enzyme action, not the first concept of metabolism.
Ibn-e-Nafeez is credited with first giving the concept of metabolism.
Bu Ali Sina is not credited with first giving the concept of metabolism here.
Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.
Division of the nucleus is called karyokinesis.
Chromosome separation occurs during nuclear division, not cytokinesis.
Mitochondria may divide, but their division is not cytokinesis.
Meiosis comes from a Greek word meaning to make smaller or reduce.
To make larger is not the meaning of meiosis.
To cut is not the meaning of meiosis.
To duplicate is not the meaning of meiosis.
0.1 cm equals 1 mm, which is not the stated resolving power of the human eye.
0.1 μm is far smaller than the human eye can resolve.
The human eye's resolution power is about 0.1 mm.
0.1 dm equals 1 cm, which is much larger than the human eye's resolving power.
